# Rome Romberger

Cloud architecture and deployment engineering. I take systems that work in a demo and
make them work in someone else's environment — which is usually a different problem.

Each project below is tagged against the capability it actually demonstrates. The tags
are a closed set validated in CI, so this page cannot quietly become a list of hobbies.

## Selected work

### [PermitPortal](https://github.com/wildgen3/permitportal)

**Deterministic obligation resolution for state business one-stop portals.**

Around twenty US states run partial business one-stop portals and about thirty run none. They fail identically: each agency owns its own form, and nobody owns the dependency order between them. An owner can find every individual requirement and still not know what to do first.

> Built clean-room from public sources. It reproduces no client system, contains no client data, and names no client. Every substantive claim traces to a public citation.

`Deployment architecture` · `Technical blocker resolution` · `Evaluation and measurement` · `Platform modernisation`

### [Canis Fortis](https://github.com/wildgen3/pawsitive-insights)

**Individual-dog re-identification and behavioural event extraction for training clubs.**

The predecessor was a demo shell: auth stubbed, nothing persisted, a dashboard rendering a hardcoded array, uploads analysed then discarded, and a learning engine that did not learn. This rebuild exists to make those claims true.

## Also

### [fedora-blueprint](https://github.com/wildgen3/fedora-blueprint)

**Idempotent, dry-runnable post-install automation reproducing a full workstation from an audited inventory.**

A working development machine is an undocumented accumulation of decisions. Rebuilding one means rediscovering all of them.

**Outcome.** Eighteen numbered idempotent modules reproduce the machine from a captured inventory, with --dry-run on every path.

`Deployment architecture` · `Workload transition`
